label: Mega-Chad highstand (modelled, experimental)
datum: metres above the geoid (mean sea level) as in Terrarium and ETOPO1 heights; not relative to the year's global ocean level

epochs.name: highstand
epochs.state: highstand at level_m, no fade or partial stage

outside_epochs: scenario inactive: the geography is unknown at that date, which is not the same as a dry lakebed; the app draws and places as it does without the flag

mask.grid: 8640 x 4320 world pixels of 2.5'; x0, y0 = column, row of the patch's north-west pixel (row 0 north, column 0 180 W)

distance.grid: 4320 x 2160 HYDE 5' cells; x0, y0 = column, row of the patch's north-west cell
distance.encoding: water_distance.json: metres = max_metres * (code / 255) ** 2, code 0 = water in the cell
distance.rule: min(static distance image, distance to the lake's cells); outside the patch the static image is exact

area_reference_km2.source: Armitage, Bristow & Drake 2015 (early to mid-Holocene Mega-Chad area)

sources.height: AWS Terrarium elevation tiles, zoom 6, mean of 3 x 3 samples per 2.5' pixel (as site_terrain.py)
sources.level: Drake & Bristow 2006, The Holocene 16: 901-911 (shorelines of palaeolake Chad; spill to the Benue at ~330 m); 329 m is the level terrain_image.py already used
sources.chronology: Armitage, Bristow & Drake 2015, PNAS 112 (28): highstand by ~11.5 ka BP, held to ~5 ka BP; calendar BP from 1950
sources.freshwater: assumed: the overflowing highstand lake is counted as fresh water (Natural Earth rivers and lakes stay as they are)

uncertainty: The shoreline is the 329 m contour of a modern 2.4 km DEM connected to Lake Chad: sediment, tectonics and DEM error since move it by km on flat ground.
The highstand was not constant between ~11.5 and ~5 ka BP; fluctuations inside the window are not modelled.
Dates are the published highstand window, not dated shorelines at every year.
Whether the shore water was fresh, brackish or seasonal is assumed, not measured.
Nothing is said outside the window: not dry, not wet.
